author: Michael Larabel
description: FreeBSD 15.2 Beta 1 is out today as the release dance kicks off in working toward the next installment of FreeBSD 15...
title: FreeBSD 15.2 Beta 1 Allows Experimental Cross-Building Of Base Packages On Linux/macOS

author: Michael Larabel
description: After years of work, ReactOS as the "open-source Windows" operating system striving for Windows program and driver compatibility now has an initial USB 3.0 driver stack in place...
title: ReactOS Lands Initial USB3 Driver Support

author: Michael Larabel
description: An interesting technical detail I noticed today from the latest AMD Linux activity is that Zen 6 processors apparently are featuring a RISC-V based Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) where in the past it was an ARM-based core...
title: A RISC-V Based TEE With AMD Zen 6 CPUs

author: Michael Larabel
description: In addition to a FAT32 optimization yielding as much as a 265x improvement that was merged for the Linux 7.4 cycle and separately another big FAT32 improvement expected for Linux 7.5, merged this week as part of the non-MM fixes for Linux 7.4-rc2 was another big FAT32 performance optimization...
title: Linux 7.4-rc2 Change Yields As Much As 162x Improvement For FAT32

author: Michael Larabel
description: With CachyOS recently having rolled out its Linux 7.3 based kernel and various other improvements plus with Omarchy 4.5 having been released this week, this article provides a look at how CachyOS and Omarchy are competing on the performance front relative to upstream Arch Linux.
title: Arch Linux vs. CachyOS vs. Omarchy 4.5 Performance Benchmarks

author: Michael Larabel
description: With the Linux kernek having phased out i486 CPU support and dropping old AMD Elan SoC code along with removing other obsolete and stagnate 32-bit x86 hardware support, some x86 32-bit clean-ups are proceeding along with being able to make the kernel depend unconditionally now on some features...
title: Linux x86 32-bit Patches Clean Old Kernel Code After Recently Removing Vintage CPUs

author: Michael Larabel
description: FEX 2611 is out for running Linux (and Wine) x86/x86_64 games/applications on AArch64 Linux. FEX 2611 brings JIT improvements while also waiting for the Linux kernel to align with the AArch64 specification and Windows on ARM and macOS Apple Silicon behavior around a particular register's usage...
title: FEX Awaits The Linux Kernel To Align With Windows & macOS On ARM Register Usage

author: Michael Larabel
description: A few months back were discussions of a Linux firmware HWE package for Ubuntu to carry updated firmware blobs under the hardware enablement (HWE) umbrella. Plus also splitting up the monolithic linux-firmware package for easing of firmware updates. Those plans didn't materialize in time for the official Ubuntu 26.10 release but are now being pursued for Ubuntu 27.04 and may then be SRU'ed into Ubuntu 26.10 and potentially Ubuntu 26.04 LTS...
title: Ubuntu Moving Ahead With Plans For Splitting Up Linux-Firmware, HWE Option

author: Michael Larabel
description: Linux kernel developers are looking at dropping the RT_GROUP_SCHED feature that is used for group scheduling of real-time tasks using cgroups...
title: Linux Developers Look To Drop RT_GROUP_SCHED As It's "Broken Beyond Repair"

author: Michael Larabel
description: The sound subsystem is seeing a "unsurprisingly high amount" fixes and device workarounds/quirks for this weekend's Linux 7.4-rc2 kernel release...
title: Sound Subsystem Seeing Lots Of Fixes & Laptop/Device Quirks For Linux 7.4-rc2

author: Michael Larabel
description: OpenCV 5.0 debuted back in June with a rewritten DNN engine and many other exciting improvements for this widely-used computer vision (CV) library. Out today is OpenCV 5.1 with tons of fixes and other incremental improvements to this important code...
title: OpenCV 5.1 Brings More AVX-512 Optimizations, Other Improvements
